# Anna: An edition becomes possible

## 1. What this prototype should do

We develop a coherent, readable web presentation for Anna, supplemented by a small interactive exploration and suitable print materials. It should address competent researchers with little technical routine and at the same time show what support an institution would have to provide for this.

The red thread is: **Anna wants to make a forgotten text readable again. Which manageable infrastructure will help her today and keep possibilities open later?** The presentation starts with the edition project and leads from there to tools, collaboration, approval and continuity.

The prototype is also an experiment with our grammar: we check the interplay of living article, precise decision-making aid, variable consequences and printed map. Only from this test do we derive changes to the general rules. The other personas are not worked out in this round.

** Scope of delivery of the first implementation:** An Anna reading section, an exploration area with three decisions and four event maps, two fully elaborated narrative situations, three main analytical graphics, a comparison of two edition versions, a small picture ensemble and five print sheets. This file plans to be implemented; images and application are not yet produced.

## 2. The first encounter: a reading track with seven stations

An associated page with sectional navigation is the starting point. Articles and exploration get their own clearly defined areas; after an excursion into a depression, the way back to the reading site remains. On small screens everything follows an understandable linear sequence.

What Readers Experience In-House 
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
The forgotten font - Interest in the text and Anna's concerns - Title, teaser, opening image; about 200–300 words about out-of-print issues, commentaries, print requests and tight time budget - "What does Anna need to start?
A good start - A manageable work path is imaginable - Short article with graphic A-G01; TEI, prepared work environment, main branch, backup and help; three foldable terms -- "What does Anna take on, where she needs support?--
3. Three decisions that are related -- Options become verifiable -- Entry into exploration; format, place of work and release path; graphic A-G02 -- "What choice will affect what later possibility?--
4. A second pair of eyes , cooperation becomes tangible as a scientific opportunity , Edited article on Mira; image detail and edition comparison A-G04; reference to C01 and R07 , "Which section and what return channel does Mira need?
5. What would be if ...? - Opportunities and risks are experienced - Four event maps, before/after, matrix and coupling A-G03; second short story about institutional changes -- "What is changing together, what must be clarified individually?"
6. More than the finished edition 的 Partial publication, teaching and revision become visible 
7. A viable next step -- A project and institutional tasks become tangible - Strategy sheet; tasks for Anna and required services; print/Export access -- "What clarification would your project now advance?--

The word numbers are production goals, not a new general rule. The entire reading distance should be accessible in about 15-20 minutes; free exploration can take longer. Technical details are available where readers need them. The six substantive questions of grammar are covered by the stations and at the end made available in a compact overview.

**Three introductions:** "Read Anna's story", "Exploring opportunities", "Materials for workshop and consulting". All lead to the same content. A directly called exploration area offers a short persona paragraph with project goal and starting position.

## 3. Image strategy: a small, coherent ensemble

The images are intended to create interest in the object, closeness to work and a lively reading rhythm. We start with two atmospheric illustrations and a technically legible detail. Color world, feeling of material and recurring work objects are unified. Anna first becomes visible through her work; a binding face is not required.

. Image ID / priority . Motif and task . Placement / Variants . . Production briefing and limits . .
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
A-B01/necessary Anna's edition work: historical print page, work notes, open work book; interest in the project aroused - kick off in broad view, close section for persona map; mobile as own image - Quiet, warm illustration with paper textures and few accents; clear focus on work. No concrete epoch claim, no readable pseudo text as source. Text and heading outside the picture --
A-B02/necessary, two perspectives on the same passage; punctual collaboration with Mira 
A-B03/necessary close-up of an edited passage and its commentary; show what Anna does professionally 
A-B04 / only after the first test, handing over an orderly inventory of work; possible accent on the change of institution, only if there is a visual gap, rather small motive as a second big opening image. No disaster picture and no equalization of retirement with loss of professional ability to act,

A genuine historical facsimile can later be added or replaced by B01 or B03. For this purpose, subject matter, conditions of use and appropriate technical explanation are first researched and tested. The first prototype can work completely with marked illustrations and a fictitious text example.

**Required accompanying data per picture:** Motif description, purpose, origin, conditions of use, marking of an AI production, alternative text, caption, permitted cut-outs and associated station. In a later image production B01 and B02 are first checked for consistency. Additional variants are created only for a concrete layout task.

**Bildrhythm:** Prelude with clear weight; afterwards a stretch of quiet text; in the Mira article a smaller offset motif; then a precise edition comparison. Not every title gets an image. A picture should invite to look or explain something. Production notes are replaced by actual media or a deliberately purely typographic design before delivery.

## 4. Graphic strategy: four clearly defined tasks

Analytical graphics are built as sharp, labelable vector graphics or directly from structured content. Technical texts remain true text. Each main graphic receives a readable list alternative and a print edition.

### A-G01 · From work to released edition

**Question:** What belongs to Anna's simple way of working, and where is consciously released?

A maximum of six main stations: editing → local check/preview → private working repository → controlled approval → publication data → web/print output. An attached backup path and a separate archive transfer are functionally distinguished. Readers:Inside can select and learn a station: What happens here? Who does it? What is stored or transmitted?

The graphic separates Anna's actions from required services with labeled areas. It explains the release threshold particularly clearly. If the space is not enough, the archiving will receive a subsequent detail section instead of a tiny additional box.

### A-G02 · Decisions with reunification of paths

**Question:** Where do different work paths reunite, and what differences remain?

The overview shows three decisions from the grammar: P01-D01 Format/Workpath, P01-D02 Workplace/Support, P01 -D03 approval/Publication Path. First, only a partial graph is opened. Format paths converge with versioned worksets, but keep their different test requirements. Hosting paths converge before the editorial approval, retain differences in access and support.

Selection of an option shows no more than three immediate consequences and access to details. Simplification, mandatory requirement and migration receive different labeled lines. The graphical layout remains as stable as possible with small changes. No free floating node network as the first view.

### A-G03 · Opportunities, risks and common cause

**Question:** What are the consequences of an event – and why?

Two separate qualitative matrix fields show selected opportunities and risks. Entries with unexplained plausibility are located in a separate visible area. The same entries stand as an understandable list. Each event map highlights only the affected entries and explains the change textually.

For the institution event, a small pairing graphic opens up: End of institutional connection → possible elimination of repo access, consultation and tool permission. Each link specifies its condition. The three consequences are confirmed individually or set to "unexplained". Prepared measures appear as possible actions; the evaluation decreases only when explicitly implemented and tested as selected measure. In the first prototype, such measures can be switched only where their effect is fully described editorially.

### A-G04 · Two versions, one technical decision

**Question:** What makes a revision comprehensible?

A short fictitious example with about 60-100 words per version: original commentary and after Mira's comment revised comment. To this end, three clear statements: What was changed? Why? Whose contribution was important? Highlighting also works without color. No simulated original source and no real Git screenshot are necessary.

A second view can show the difference between former citable approval and new version. The example combines collaboration and revision opportunity and is reused in print like Web. The professional sample passage is completely edited before technical implementation.

## 5. Dynamics: a small, explainable state model

### Initial situation

P01-S00 remains the documented assumption: Anna works mainly alone; TEI with a prepared environment is preferred; institutional access and advice are initially available, longer term conditions unexplained. Private work and controlled public approval are separate. Planned security and handover are not presented as already implemented.

A visible note explains: "You're exploring a fictitious project. The starting point can be changed. "Selected scenarios are not advice on an actually tested service.

### Three first-scale decisions

. . field . . selection . . What changes visibly
| --- | --- | --- |
的 Work format 
• Working environment • Uni-GitLab with consulting / Uni-GITLab only as hosting / other suitable service with clear support • Responsibilities, support questions and handover needs; GitHub prior experience as an additional optional context
Intention to release 

The hybrid format option is initially described as a deepening. "Other service" receives an explanation with GitHub as an example, without assuming current tariffs or service commitments. The specific publication location is visible as a consistently open carrier question; a second complete hosting configurator would be too extensive for this test.

### Four Event Cards

"Event" "Initial state and direct consequences" "Learning point / completion"
| --- | --- | --- |
"Mira offers reading back to the page "S02 enabled; C01 becomes concrete, R07 makes integration and support visible "Select matching cut-out and return channel; name recognition and responsibility
"Anna is planning a course----specific appointment activated S04; C03 and release exam become relevant--limited teaching version and public partial publication consciously distinguish---
"Anna's university connection ends" "First only event; access, advice and license each further available / ends / unresolved" "Priorize common cause with conditional consequences, X01/X02 and help; complete test case S01 by default loadable"
"The working computer falls out of the event has occurred; it can be selected whether the last version was externally matched and independently checked for backup - Distinguished local changes differ from existing repo data and recoverability; no entry evaluation of the defect that has already occurred -

Events are examined individually against the chosen starting position in this round. "Explore another event" replaces the previous event and says so explicitly. This avoids unfounded combination effects. The three decisions remain unchanged. A separate button resets everything to S00. Later multiple events are a possible extension after testing.

**Each change provides four things:** modified acceptance; affected steps in the work path; previously/after with justification; next Action and responsible role. Focus and reading position remain unchanged. No automatic jumps, no success bar and no total value for "good Git usage".

**Result:** A strategy sheet contains initial values, current decisions, active event, open questions, action status, task distribution and version. print and downloadable text export exactly this condition. Operation data is not required for the test function; the first version works without accounts or background transmission.

For terms first, six editorially verified short texts are sufficient: Git, TEI, Work/Publication Repo, Commit/Release, Validation, Backup/Archive. Each offers a short definition → Meaning for Anna → Limit. Product-specific statements are currently checked before concrete recommendation. This is part of the later implementation, no already completed research.

The existing P01 IDs remain decisive. A-B and A-G are production identifiers for assets, not a second content logic. A small structured Anna file contains decisions, scenario values, consequences and references. Texts and graphics are supplied consistently from this. Articles remain editorially related texts; they are not composed of matrix lines.

## 7. Printing materials: small enough to really test them

1. **Persona map A5, two pages:** Project sales, starting position, guiding question; back minimum target and support.
2. **Architecture sheet A4 crosswise:** A-G01, release threshold, backup and archive, roles.
3. **Four event cards A6 on an A4 sheet:** Occasion, a question, relevant IDs and reference to follow-up sheet.
4. **Current follow-up and strategy sheet A4, two pages if required:** exact state of exploration, before/after, measures and open questions.
5. **Mira article as its own reading version:** Interim headings, edition comparison and matching images; length determines the number of pages.

The print view does not receive an interactive ballast. All explanations required for understanding are output. An expression of a changed state must clearly name it. Articles and cards are checked separately; a working screen page does not yet prove a good print edition.

. Step . . Work . . Final criterion . .
| --- | --- | --- |
1. Tighten the content and rules of R1–R6, edit the edition example and state rules; preform each output 的 All controls have understandable consequences; no unexplained values are rated covertly
2. Designing a typical reading route 
3. Create images and graphics together, B03/G04 technically precise, G01–G03 as labeled graphics, readability, image purpose, consistent style, alternative texts and origin documented
4. Build a continuous prototype, explore, same state data for graphics and results, all three decisions and four individual events work with reset and open status
5. print and check accessibility 的 maps, strategy sheet, articles; keyboard, magnification, small view and screen reader 
6. Test and revise grammar - Collect observations, locate problems, specific rule change - Change protocol separates grammar problem, Anna content and implementation error

A local or statically executable implementation with limited interaction logic is sufficient for this scope. In actual web production, the appropriate existing website environment is chosen. Technical architectural decisions follow the state export, print requirements and accessibility. Publication is a separate step after final preview and verification.

## 9. Test: What questions should Anna answer for our grammar?

A first formative round with about four to six people is a work proposal, not a representative study. Including: Edition subject with little Git experience, person with his own project project, teacher or student as well as infrastructure/consultation perspective. At least one session should check the use with keyboard or assistive technology. If these perspectives are still missing, this remains an open test task.

- Test task - Watch possible consequence for grammar -
| --- | --- | --- |
"Read the introduction and reflect Anna's concerns in her own words" "Are professional competence, pressure desire and short time remembered? Where does interest or distance arise? "Change narrative length, teaser and image task" "
To explain what Mira needs to see, Is limited approval understood? Does the episode help in factual judgment?
Change Uni-Connection - Will three conditional consequences be detected? Are unknown and "end" differentiated? - Simplify or specify coupling and condition model
Is a dependency misunderstood as automatism? Is it possible to revise edges, convergence and permanent state display?
- Play computer failure - Are reconciliation, backup and recovery kept apart? - Reshape architecture and event formulations
Can anyone without a web context explain the state and next step?
To name required infrastructure performance is individual responsibility associated with concrete support? 

After a short free reading follow these tasks. Capture: false expectations, stumbling, backsliding information, omitted sections, helpful picture/text passages and open questions. Reading joy and empathy are explored by inquiries: "Where did you want to read more?", "What was too schematic for you?", "Which situation could you understand?" Clicking a button often proves neither understanding nor interest.

**Decision before this round:** Technical statements comprehensible; all controls have a visible effect or explanation; no unknown value is set low; the print output agrees with the current state; essential ways are understandable without mouse and without graphics. Clear errors are fixed before testing. The user test itself is still pending.

## 10. Return to the general grammar

For each observation is recorded: location and used state → observed problem → suspected cause → proposed change → countercheck. Changes received one of these categories:

- **Anna content:** Example to abstract, missing information or unrealistic assumption; initially only change case text.
- **Design/implementation:** wrong order, unreadable section, misunderstood operation; repair concrete representation.
- **General grammar:** Material boundaries, object model, interaction rule or media change are fundamentally unsuitable; formulate general rule as proposed changes.

A finding of Anna gives rise to a hypothesis for other personas. Before generalisation, at least one case with several parties or higher protection needs is examined. The three other personas remain provisional for this purpose; we do not have to develop them in this round.

**Result of the round:** revised Anna prototype, prioritized open questions and a short change protocol to grammar 0.3.0. The next grammar version takes over only well-founded changes and documents what has so far been tested on Anna alone.

## 11. Specific starting point

First, entry, Mira article and edition comparison are worked out together with the simple work path. This section already contains empathy, reading joy, image/text change, precise graphics and a real decision. Afterwards, event exploration, matrix, institutional transfer and print export follow. Thus, a coherent experience grows, whose first parts are immediately verifiable.

The first production list includes **three required images or image details, four analytical graphics, three decisions, four individually detectable events and five types of printed material**. Additional motifs and functions are only added when a concrete gain in knowledge or understanding becomes apparent.
